en: Taal Volcano is located in Batangas and is one of the smallest active volcanoes in the world, featuring a main crater lake on Volcano Island.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley region.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering an area of about 911 square kilometers southeast of Manila.
The Philippine eagle is a critically endangered bird of prey endemic to the tropical forests of the island of Mindanao.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected marine sanctuary known for its pristine coral atolls.
Batanes is the northernmost province of the Philippines, characterized by its rolling limestone hills and traditional stone houses built to withstand typhoons.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical cone-shaped mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The tamaraw is a small buffalo endemic to the island of Mindoro and is currently one of the rarest bovines globally.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago for agricultural use.
The Philippine Trench is a major oceanic trench in the Pacific Ocean, reaching its deepest point at the Galathea Depth.
